name: blasius_flat_plate
title: Blasius boundary layer over a flat plate
summary: Solution of the classic Blasius equation of the laminar boundary layer over a flat plate: the third-order ODE f''' + 0.5*f*f'' = 0 is integrated with the Integral function between the similarity coordinates eta = 0 and eta = 5, the shooting parameter f''(0) being the classical 0.33206; the dimensionless velocity profile f'(eta) is mapped to the dimensional coordinates x and y for air at 25 °C.
language_features: prime notation in the variable names (not supported by CoolSolve)

verification.summary: Runnable variant vs the EES stored solution of the binary source: 16 common variables, 4 differ (rtol=0.001), max 2.91e-03 on mu (EES vs CoolProp air viscosity). Newton shooting on f''(0) with the model gives 0.33205734, the classic Blasius value 0.3320573362.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/EES_library/Blasius.EES (16 decoded variables) and its parametric table (501 rows); classic Blasius value f''(0) = 0.3320573362 (Blasius 1908, in White, Viscous Fluid Flow)
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 16 common variables, 4 differ (rtol=0.001), only in EES: 0, only in CoolSolve: 5 (the renamed derivatives w_1, w_1_0, w_2, w_2_0, w_3; the extractor did not decode the EES names that carry the prime notation). Largest relative difference 2.91e-03 on mu (1.84874e-05 Pa.s in EES against 1.84337e-05 Pa.s in CoolProp); nu, u and u_infinity follow from it (2.8e-03). No variable excluded. The EES parametric table (step 0.01) gives w = 3.283289405 and w' = 0.991547628 at eta = 5 against 3.283295772 and 0.991547343 (1.94e-06 and 2.87e-07); the stored EES solution is the one of the fixed-step integration of EES (1.92e-04 on w). Shooting on f''(0) (Newton on f'(eta) - 1 at the end of the integration, eta = 30, with the model) gives 0.332057344620 (RK4, step 0.1) and 0.332057336215 with an accurate adaptive integration (DOP853, rtol = 1e-13).
